raw_response:
I've been farming these 7 mu in Quzhou for over twenty years. Never went to school, can't read much, but I know my land. My husband works construction in Handan when he can, so most days it's me and my mother-in-law doing the farm work. We can't afford to mess around with fancy new things — I do what my neighbors do, and what has filled our bellies in the past.

I keep 5 mu for wheat and maize, same as always. Wheat goes in around October 10th, about 30 jin of seed per mu — I save my own seed from the good ears, it's an improved variety that the village seed station sells. I rotary till before sowing. For fertilizer, I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — the one they call "special" with the blue label, about 18-22-5 or something like that, I don't know the numbers but I know the bag. Then when the wheat turns green in March, if it looks yellow I broadcast another half bag of ammonium bicarbonate, and at jointing I might add a bit more urea. Better to put a bit too much than too little — last year my cousin cut back and her wheat was stunted. I irrigate four times: winter water, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Water costs money but you can't skip it. For sprays, I do herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice when I see aphids, and fungicide once if the weather stays wet.

Maize goes in the same 5 mu right after wheat harvest in early June — there's barely a week, sometimes less, so I no-till plant straight into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, one small package per mu, usually Nongda or Denghai. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting, the high-nitrogen kind, 28-6-6. Irrigate twice if the summer is dry — seedling stage and big-flare stage. Herbicide once, insecticide twice for corn borer. Maize is easier than wheat.

I put 2 mu in cotton because the price has been around 3 yuan per jin the last few years, and Lao Wang down the road always gets good money from his cotton. Cotton is hard work — lots of picking and spraying — but on 2 mu I can manage with family labor. I rotary till in mid-April and plant an improved variety, about 2-3 jin seed per mu. Basal fertilizer is one bag of compound per mu, and I topdress at flowering. Irrigate three times. Cotton needs spraying almost every week in summer — insects love it — so maybe 10 times total with insecticide, herbicide, and fungicide. I expect about 1000 jin per mu of seed cotton if the weather cooperates.

I thought about stevia like some people in the next village, but I don't know anyone who can teach me, and if the buyer doesn't show up, I'm stuck with a field of weeds. Wheat and maize I can always eat or sell. Cotton I understand. That's my year.
